name: Pixel-to-Voxel
summary: Flat pixel dashboards extrude into a voxel skyline; the anomalous tower ejects a coral voxel and leaves dashed ghost cubes.
look: Isometric voxels on a pale floor lattice with soft ambient shading. Teal towers, cream/grey filler cubes, one coral rogue voxel with dashed ghost outlines.

components.name: Pixel grid
components.role: the UI rasterised into square pixels — the flat “before” state

components.name: Extrude ripple
components.role: per-cell depth 0→1 radiating from the centre

components.name: Metric tower
components.role: a voxel column per metric; height encodes value

components.name: Rogue voxel
components.role: the coral cube that ejects from the anomalous tower

components.name: Ghost cubes
components.role: dashed coral outlines of the missing height (−18 %)

components.name: Voxel button
components.role: flat face + 12 px solid ledge, reads as a physical block

motion.name: Ripple extrude
motion.how: delay = distance × 0.015 s, back.out(2) 0.4 s; the wave front crosses the centre on the downbeat

motion.name: Gravity drop
motion.how: cubes fall power2.in 0.25 s + one small bounce, one cube per eighth note at 120 BPM

motion.name: Camera orbit
motion.how: linear 20° yaw across 8 bars; never eased, so the beat-locked cube hits carry the rhythm

story: Hook: a flat pixel mosaic of dashboards rasterises in, one dipping on Friday. Reveal: the floor ripples up into 3D on the drop, the teal centre tower rises and the Acme mark lands on it. Proof: metric towers grow; the checkout tower ejects a coral voxel leaving ghost cubes, and a card reads “Checkout conversion −18% · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231” with “Roll back”. CTA: “Every metric. Every minute.” beside a small voxel stack and “Start free”.
adapt: Rasterise your own dashboard into the opening mosaic, then extrude the 4–5 numbers your product cares about as towers; the thing your product catches is the tower that loses its top voxel.

references.note: pixel-to-voxel drop effect with Three.js + Rapier

fit.risk: Needs Three.js with baked, deterministic physics; keep to ≤ 5 towers so labels stay legible.
